react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary pathway-analysis paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of galactose metabolism. RaMP multi-DB ORA (SMPDB/KEGG/Reactome/WikiPathways) identifies Galactosemia (SMPDB:SMP00182) and Galactose Metabolism (SMPDB:SMP00043; KEGG:map00052) as the top two hits with FDR = 1.06×10⁻¹³, a 1 086-fold enrichment. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA independently confirms KEGG:hsa00052 with raw p = 5.16×10⁻⁸, rank 1. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis on the human_mfn empirical-compound network corroborates with MUMM:galactose_metabolism (p = 0.0083, rank 5) and extends the signal to the related Starch and Sucrose Metabolism module (MUMM:starch_and_sucrose_metabolism, p = 0.0072, rank 4). Five structurally resolved driver metabolites anchor this convergence: sucrose (KEGG:C00089), galactinol (KEGG:C01235), galactitol (KEGG:C01697), glycerol (KEGG:C00116), and myo-inositol (KEGG:C00137) — all resolved to unique InChIKey first-blocks by reconcile_inchikey with zero conflicts. An independent Reactome ORA cluster targets aspirin ADME (R-HSA-9749641, FDR = 1.82×10⁻⁴), linking the pharmaceutical inputs (acetaminophen KEGG:C06804, aspirin KEGG:C01405) to xenobiotic metabolism. Cross-paradigm consensus is strongest for galactose metabolism, which appears as a top-3 hit across all three paradigms. Farnesyl pyrophosphate (KEGG:C00448) and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (KEGG:C20319) are structurally coherent with the m/z space but fall below the FDR threshold in ORA; their annotation is consistent with the N-glycan biosynthesis hit in Mummichog (rank 6). The biological story is a treatment-induced reprogramming of carbohydrate flux through the Leloir pathway, with galactose-family sugars (sucrose, galactinol, galactitol) and myo-inositol as the principal driver metabolites.
